I have investigated and resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery (`WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)`).

### Root Cause
When multi-alias fast-path deletion was refactored in [`SQLDeleteCompiler`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-51kf5huc/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412), `single_alias` was defined as:
```python
sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1
```
For queries without any filters or joins (such as `Model.objects.all()`), `self.query.alias_map` was empty (`{}`) because `self.query.get_initial_alias()` had never been called. Consequently, `sum(...)` returned `0`, causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False`. The compiler then treated the delete query as a multi-table query and generated a subquery on the primary key.

### Fix
In [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-51kf5huc/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1413), ensure the base table is initialized in `alias_map` if all alias refcounts in `alias_map` are 0 (following the convention in `SQLCompiler.setup_query`):
```python
if all(self.query.alias_refcount[a] == 0 for a in self.query.alias_map):
    self.query.get_initial_alias()
```
This ensures `single_alias` evaluates to `True` for `Model.objects.all().delete()`, generating `DELETE FROM <table>` directly without a subquery.
